evidence: src/domain/order.ts: advance() calls nextStateOf() and cancel() calls isCancellable(), both from src/domain/order-state.ts; the transition tables are not copied into Order.
src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: reserve() calls product.canReserve(quantity), the one definition in src/domain/product.ts, before calling product.reserve(quantity).
src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: the constructor takes `private readonly products: ProductRepository`, and data is reached only through this.products.findById and this.products.save.
src/domain/order-item.ts checks that quantity > 0; src/domain/product.ts checks that initialStock >= 0. These are different rules.
src/domain/order-repository.ts, src/domain/product-repository.ts and src/domain/id-generator.ts are port interfaces only and contain no implementation.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All nine files serve one concern: the order-and-stock domain. That covers the entities (Order, OrderItem, Product), the order states (order-state.ts), the domain errors, the ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, IdGenerator) and a domain service (StockReservationService).

Each rule is written once. Order transitions live only in order-state.ts, in NEXT_STATE and CANCELLABLE, and Order.advance and Order.cancel call nextStateOf and isCancellable instead of copying them. The stock-sufficiency rule lives only in Product.canReserve. StockReservationService.reserve checks every product with that same method before reserving any of them, so that it reserves all items or none. The only repeated text is the error message 'Insufficient stock for product ...', which is not a copied rule. The quantity check in OrderItem (positive integer) and the stock check in Product (non-negative integer) are different rules, not a duplicate.

Persistence goes only through the module's own port: StockReservationService gets ProductRepository through its constructor and uses only findById and save. No database, ORM or query client is used directly. No file goes around the module's own abstractions.
